questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture, the location and surrounding nature and mountains, the possibility to study sociology in another national context

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: When in direct contact with staff, for example at introduction days, quite easy - but when e-mailing, they took a long time to respond

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The introduction days, and the materials provided here, where quite helpfull

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite difficult - I was rather lucky to get in contact with another erasmus student who set me in contact with the landlady she had just found. I would recommend starting to look early on, and to keep an eye out for scams or apartments in really bad conditions - especially some apartments that were only rented out to erasmus students had terrible landlords and were in really bad condition!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The city itself is quite small, so if you dont mind walking 15-20 minutes to the center, you can also look for apartments outside the historic city center

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It mostly worked through the OLA, but in the first couple of week you could also just show up for classes you were interested in, and talk to the professors

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Talking to the professors in person was quite helpful! Writing to the mobility-staff was not, as they took forever to reply

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Completely succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bear in mind that they don't offer that many courses in english and that some of these courses are taught at the same time - so chances are that you will have to change your original pick of courses once the semester starts

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It changed a lot depending on the subject and the professor

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite different! Many of the professors refused to share their lecture slides, and some of the exams where written in hand

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociology of Collective action
Space and Culture
Cultural Analytics
People, Politics and the Planet
Global and Transnational History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: People, Politics and the Planet - if you are at all into environmental studies (and even if you are not) I would recommend this course! Professor Parks is the best!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things are less expensive than in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The ESN arranged a lot of activities, trips etc. And there was the possibility to sign up for fitness membership and sports teams through the university. But I think the teams filled up quite quickly.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The ESN ski trip was great! Quite cheap for 4 days of skiing and fun apres!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The Dolomites !! Whether skiing, hiking etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the people you have classes with

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They were all quite friendly and open - and the ritual of aperitivo is of course amazing

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It can be difficult to find a nice accomodation, it can be difficult to get all the courses that you want - but it's worth it!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Really getting to know the locals + being able to spend as much time in the mountains as I wanted

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding five english speaking courses that I found interesting and that were not taught at the same time

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
